protocol.base_model: N=30,K=100 random binary memories; k=10; neuronal Euler update; finite astrocyte gain uses positivity/simplex-preserving exponential replicator update; instantaneous control sets p=softmax(f/T) before each neuronal update; hard Hamming is sign(x) versus target.
protocol.stationary_confirmation: Official-style six-bit corrupted target, Time=10, corrected endpoint, 500 common-random-number paired realizations/cell. Numpy deterministic pattern/query generation used for this confirmation; both variants receive identical patterns/query per pair.
protocol.transient_precondition: Start x at exact stored pattern 0 and p uniform, run each model for 2 s so a correct previously retrieved context is established. Preserve each model's p across perturbation.
protocol.noisy_query_reset: At t=2 replace x by a fresh ±1 corrupted version of the same target, preserving p. This tests temporal filtering/context persistence rather than stationary endpoint retrieval.
protocol.query_switch: At t=2 replace x by stored pattern 1 with six flipped bits, preserving p. This tests hysteresis cost under a true context switch.
protocol.validation: For one n=9,tau_p=1 noisy-query trajectory, direct PyTorch float32 and compiled Numba implementations matched the full hard-error readout traces exactly for both finite and instantaneous variants.

actions: Confirmed all strongest non-tau_p=0.3 stationary screen candidates at 500 paired realizations; none retained a beneficial 95% bootstrap interval excluding zero.
Moved to nonstationary perturbations and found a large reproducible same-context noise-filtering benefit from persistent finite astrocyte gain state versus instantaneous softmax recomputation.
Ran the complementary true-context-switch intervention and found the same persistence creates a large switching/hysteresis cost.
Mapped noisy-query robustness over corruption severity and several finite tau_p values; the effect survives from mild to severe corruption in the tested synthetic regime.

stationary_non_tau03_confirmation.interpretation: The apparent finite-tau stationary endpoint advantages from the 50-run screen did not survive 500-pair confirmation. Across all prioritized non-0.3 candidates, every 95% interval crossed zero.

transient_same_context_filtering.tau_p_robustness: For nine-bit same-target resets at tau_p={0.03,0.1,0.3,1,3}, 300 paired realizations each, the finite-state model reached mean hard error 0 by 50 ms at every tested tau_p, while the instantaneous control remained at mean 10.797 bits by 2 s. This should be interpreted as benefit from carried gain state/hysteresis in this intervention, not evidence that a particular slow tau_p is uniquely optimal.

transient_context_switch_cost.switch: pattern0 settled for 2 s -> pattern1 query with six flipped bits

interpretation: The stationary endpoint search still does not support a robust accuracy benefit from finite astrocyte kinetics over instantaneous softmax.

A different mechanism appears under temporal perturbation: preserving the gain state across a corrupted observation acts as a strong context prior/noise filter and prevents instantaneous reallocation into spurious memories.

The same persistence is strongly harmful when the observation is a genuine context switch. This establishes a synthetic stability-plasticity tradeoff: gain-state inertia filters nuisance noise but creates switch hysteresis.

Because nine-bit filtering was similar across tau_p=0.03 to 3 after a 2 s settled precondition, the demonstrated effect is primarily evidence for persistent state/carryover, not yet for a finely tuned biological timescale.

The interventions are new computational tests, not experiments from the paper and not evidence for a microscopic astrocyte mechanism. They are limited to the paper's small random associative-memory regime and hard state resets.
exact_next_action: Replace hard x resets with a controlled external-query/noise drive and evaluate a stochastic environment with nuisance-corruption probability q and true-context-switch hazard h. Sweep tau_p and compare cumulative retrieval loss, switch latency and false-switch rate against instantaneous softmax and an explicit generic leaky-softmax prior. Test whether finite replicator dynamics offers anything beyond generic temporal smoothing, and estimate the tau_p optimum as a function of q/h. Preserve source-qualified scope, positivity-preserving integration and common-random-number paired evaluation.
